prompt.context: Royal Health Services is a regional healthcare system operating several hospitals and clinics in the Midwest. Due to market fragmentation and increased costs of providing care, their profit margin has continued to decrease. The board of directors has asked you to develop a strategy to increase profitability over the next two years.
prompt.question: Develop a strategy to increase Royal Health Services' profitability over the next two years.

clarifying_info.q: How many hospitals and clinics does Royal Health operate, and where?
clarifying_info.a: Royal Health operates 7 hospitals and 40+ clinics in Missouri, Kansas, and Nebraska. The clinics are less of a focus of this case.

clarifying_info.q: What levels of care and patient demographics does Royal Health serve?
clarifying_info.a: Royal Health provides all levels of care to all ages.

clarifying_info.q: Can Royal Health attract patients from outside the region?
clarifying_info.a: Royal Health is not nationally known for the care provided and is therefore unlikely to attract patients from outside the region.

clarifying_info.q: What is happening in the broader healthcare industry?
clarifying_info.a: The healthcare industry has had considerable consolidation in recent years. Regulatory changes and pressure from payers have made it increasingly difficult for individual hospitals and smaller health systems to maintain profitability.

exhibits.title: Regional Health System Comparison
exhibits.shows: A table comparing Royal Health Services against three other health systems on 2016 revenue, 2016 operating income, number of hospitals, states of operation, and number of employees.

Health System #2.states: CO, KS, IL, IN, KY, OH, PA, TX, WA

exhibits.title: 2016 Corporate Shared Services – % of Total Operating Expense
exhibits.shows: Two tables: (1) a breakdown of five corporate shared service functions as a percentage of total operating expense for Health System #3 and Royal Health Services; (2) the combined total 2016 operating expense for a merged Royal Health and Health System #3.

framework: Revenue lever: Pricing is highly regulated; volume growth unlikely given regional constraints — limited upside internally
Cost lever: Explore internal cost reduction (labor, SG&A, IT, supplier contracts, physician contracts, facilities)
Competitive landscape: Assess market fragmentation and peer positioning to identify structural options
M&A / consolidation: Evaluate acquisition or merger targets to gain scale and improve margin
Scale benefits: Larger health systems achieve higher margins through shared service centralization and bargaining power

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate the operating margin for each organization and identify what they suggest about Royal Health's competitive position.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate operating margin (Operating Income / Revenue) for all four organizations and note that Royal Health has the lowest margin at 3%. Health System #2's 8% margin should signal that scale drives higher profitability. Candidate should also map geographic overlap: Health System #1 overlaps in KS and MO; Health System #2 has no overlap; Health System #3 overlaps only in MO. This should drive candidates toward M&A targeting Health System #3 (new markets + some overlap) or Health System #1 (full overlap but limited scale).

math.answer: Royal Health Services has the lowest operating margin at 3%; Health System #2 achieves 8% at scale.

questions.prompt: After concluding that a merger with Health System #3 is the preferred path, what are the ways to create value through this merger?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm multiple value-creation categories: (1) Synergies — centralize corporate shared services (admin, finance, legal, IT, revenue cycle), reduce duplicate capital investments, consolidate medical services in overlapping regions; (2) Scale — grow market share, gain bargaining power with suppliers and health plans, access new markets (IL, OK); (3) Growth and quality — integrated care, standardized clinical processes, improved patient experience and reputation.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, quantify the potential cost savings from consolidating corporate shared services after a merger with Health System #3.
questions.guidance: The five shared service categories together equal 35% of total operating expense for both organizations. By adopting the lowest percentage in each category the combined entity should reduce this to 28% of total operating expense. Use $4,000M (rounded) as total combined operating expense. Savings = (35% - 28%) x $4,000M = $280M. An excellent candidate will also pull Exhibit 1 data to calculate the new combined margin: combined revenue = $2,400M + $1,800M = $4,200M; combined operating income before savings = $72M + $90M = $162M (pre-merger margin ~3.86%); combined operating income with $280M savings = $162M + $280M = $442M; new margin = $442M / $4,200M = ~10.5% (casebook notes 12.9% using $3,720M op expense approach). Note: number of employees data is unnecessary as hospital size within each system varies.

math.setup: Take the lowest shared-service percentage across the two organizations in each category to get the post-merger benchmark, then compute savings on combined $4,000M operating expense.
steps: Lowest rates by category: Finance 3%, HR 4%, IT 8%, Legal 4%, Revenue Cycle 9% → total 28%
Current blended rate: 35% of $4,000M = $1,400M in shared service costs
Post-merger rate: 28% of $4,000M = $1,120M in shared service costs
[Stretch] Combined operating margin: $442M / $4,200M ≈ 10.5% (casebook cites ~12.9% using $3,720M expense base)
math.answer: $280M in annual cost savings from shared service consolidation; combined operating expenses reduced from ~$4,000M to ~$3,720M.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some of the ways to create value through a merger with Health System #3?

categories.name: Synergies
ideas: Centralize corporate shared services (admin, finance, legal, IT, revenue cycle) to reduce headcount and infrastructure
Reduce level of initial and future capital investments needed
Consolidate duplicative medical services in overlapping MO markets to improve patient experience and reduce cost

categories.name: Scale
ideas: Grow market share across a larger geographic footprint (adding IL and OK)
Increase bargaining power with medical suppliers and health plans
Diversify revenue base across more markets

categories.name: Growth and Quality
ideas: Integrate care delivery across the combined organization
Standardize clinical processes to improve outcomes and efficiency
Improve reputation and patient experience to attract more patients within the expanded region

recommendation: Recommend that the Board of Directors move forward with further exploring a merger with Health System #3

The merger offers scale benefits, geographic expansion into IL and OK, some overlap in MO to consolidate, and an estimated $280M in annual shared service cost savings — improving combined operating margin materially from Royal's current 3%
risks: Anti-trust and regulatory review may delay or block the merger
Synergies may not be fully realized due to integration challenges or cultural differences
Current regulatory climate creates uncertainty (e.g., potential changes to reimbursement under ACA reform)
next_steps: Announce that a merger agreement is being pursued and sign a definitive agreement to seek regulatory approval
Complete full due diligence on Health System #3's financials, operations, and liabilities
Consider any necessary rebranding for the combined entity
